sources.title: Pull Up to 7-Eleven in Forza Horizon 6
sources.text: Every good drive has a convenience store stop along the way somewhere. Starting today, that stop becomes possible for a limited time inside Forza Horizon 6 . XBOX and 7-Eleven, Inc. are teaming up on the new Horizon Meets update – as well as releasing a merch collection and an in-store offer across the US and Canada. If you’re new to the Evolving World, it’s how Forza Horizon 6 keeps changing under your tires. For the Horizon Meets update, Playground Games is dropping a storefront inspired by 7-Eleven into the world, featuring a themed Car Meet. Head to the game’s Nangan region, bring friends, park the rides you’ve made, and download the car liveries and tuning setups on display from other players. Beyond the store itself, you can rep 7-Eleven in Forza Horizon 6’s Japan in a number of new ways: Konbini Prop Pack : 7-Eleven-themed items you can use to dress up your Estate, your Garages, and your own custom tracks in EventLab. This includes the entire konbini! Clerk Uniform : New avatar clothing inspired by the uniform worn by 7-Eleven clerks in Japan, in case you want to look like you actually work at the store. Egg Salad Sandwich Collectible : Smash 20 Egg Salad Sandwich Collectibles (find them near the 7-Eleven Evolving World Car Meet) during Autumn and earn Points completion towards the Festival Playlist, as well as a new Forza LINK reward. There’s far more coming in the Horizon Meets update – check out Forza.net for all the details. Through October 27, fans in the US and Canada can grab an exclusive in-game 7-Eleven Toyota Supra GR livery and a free Slurpee drink with the purchase of an XBOX Gift Card with 7Rewards at participating 7-Eleven stores. The real-life7-Eleven x Forza Horizon 6 merch drop arrives October 8, exclusively on 7Collection.com with hoodies, shirts, hats, and accessories featuring Toyota cars from the game in original Japanese-inspired art styles. The Horizon Meets update is available to download now, with the Festival Playlist and Evolving World content rolling out today. Grab a Slurpee drink, pick up an XBOX Gift Card, and we’ll see you in the parking lot.

sources.title: Forza Horizon 6 Is Finally Coming to PS5 in January Alongside First Expansion
sources.text: Forza Horizon 6 is finally coming to PS5 in January, and it will launch alongside a major expansion to the game. A new trailer has confirmed that Forza Horizon 6 will race on to PS5 on January 26. It will arrive on the same day and date as the game's first major expansion, though no details have been revealed on what that will look like. As was the case with the Xbox and PC version of the game, players can pre-order the Premium Edition for extra goodies, including five days of early access to the game on PS5. Players who preorder any version of the game on PS5 will also get a pre-tuned Ferrari J50. The news of the game's release date comes after rumors that Forza Horizon 6 would miss its initial 2026 release window for PS5. The news confirms that to be the case, but it will launch just in time to remove itself from GTA 6's blast radius. This should ensure it performs well on PS5 and give the game a healthy audience. Forza Horizon 5 was a massive hit on PS5 when it was released on the console last year, so there is a strong demand for its sequel. IGN gave Forza Horizon 6 a 10/10 in its review , praising it for it dense map, technical achievements, and well-paced campaign. "I’ll always concede Forza Horizon 3 may forever be my favourite open-world racer, because who doesn’t love driving around their own backyard, but make no mistake: Forza Horizon 6 is unequivocally the best," reads an excerpt from our review. "The new standard in open-world racing is here, and it’s a gundamn masterpiece." Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. sources.title: GTA 6 Reveals a Handful of Radio Stations, DJs, and Songs Ahead of Release
sources.text: Rockstar Games has launched a new website which allows you to listen to some of the radio stations and songs that will be featured in GTA 6 . Rockstar said GTA 6 will feature the "biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet," and, as always, has hired a number of celebrities such as Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey to host the stations. As for some of the things you'll be able to listen to, here are all of the stations and some of the songs that Rockstar has revealed so far. Cocoteo FM: Leonida's home for the best of modern Latin music. Hosted by El Martillo (voiced by Bad Bunny) and La Gata (voiced by RaiNao) and featuring everything from bachata and merengue to dembow and reggaeton – Cocoteo FM is el party que nunca se apaga . Back Country Radio: MW (voiced by Morgan Wallen) and Delta Dawne (voiced by Lana Del Rey) blast renegade country music to the Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, and beyond. Stay tuned for Back Country’s roving reporter, swamp meteorologist, and Delta’s not-so-secret lover Mud Dog Mike (voiced by Jeremy Dufrene) checking in from the driver’s seat of his Grassrivers airboat. AfroBank FM: Turn up the gbedu with Burna (voiced by Burna Boy) and Palmsy (voiced by Palms Trax), AfroBank FM's dynamic duo curating the best in African music, from 20th-century classics and undiscovered gems to contemporary sounds like amapiano, 3-step, and more. The Chamber 106.6: Crushing metal has landed in Leonida. Jump in the pit with DJ Kerry (voiced by Kerry King) and DJ Tom (voiced by Tom Araya) for classic metal from the ‘80s and beyond as they channel Leonida’s deep metal roots. Flash FM: The Vice City institution that delivers the best in pop music with Robyn (voiced by herself) and Alex (voiced by Alex Consani) — guaranteed to make you dance no matter where you find yourself in the Goodtime State. Dirty South Classics: A little southern hospitality from Trick (voiced by Trick Daddy) and Trina (voiced by herself), blasting regional rap and hip-hop classics. From the beach to the block, nobody reps Leonida and the South like they do. This small selection does confirm there will be a wide variety of music, as some of the music featured includes the likes of Charli XCX, Bad Bunny, MGMT, DJ Khaled, and Black Sabbath. It's unclear if Rockstar will reveal the entire list of tracks in GTA 6 before launch, but this does provide a pretty good idea of what we'll be getting on November 19. Additionally, Rockstar released a small batch of new screenshots and confirmed that GTA 6 will feature the ability to listen to on-demand podcasts and radio stations on foot by using a pair of headphones and your smartphone. This is a massive feature that fans have wanted for years, as the radio has previously been confined to your vehicles and inside of select buildings. However, now players will be able to listen to music freely when they're in combat, exploring on foot, and more. In September, Rockstar Games confirmed that it will release an album comprised of original music, made for GTA 6. So far, Rockstar has confirmed original songs from Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen, Keith Richards, and more. The entire tracklist has yet to be revealed, but it wouldn't be surprising if we hear more about the album later this month or early November ahead of the game's launch. All of this news is coming just hours after 25 minutes of new GTA 6 gameplay leaked on the internet . The new footage comes from Cyberleek, who was responsible for leaking a ton of GTA gameplay in August. Rockstar has yet to respond to the new footage, but is likely hoping that the news around the game's radio station serves as an ample distraction. IGN also posted a full transcript of its interview with Rob Nelson, the studio co-head of Rockstar North . Nelson demoed GTA 6 for IGN earlier this summer and revealed a variety of new information regarding the game in our conversation with him. GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5. Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.text: You can preview the game’s first six radio stations now, including everything from rap to country.﻿ You can preview the game’s first six radio stations now, including everything from rap to country.﻿ Music is always a major part of a Grand Theft Auto game, and Rockstar Games says GTA VI will have the series’ “biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet.” There will be at least six radio stations players can listen to in vehicles or on foot, ranging from talk radio to classic rock: Cocoteo FM, Back Country Radio, AfroBank FM, The Chamber 106.6, Flash FM, and Dirty South Classics. sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: GTA 6 radio stations revealed alongside a series first: in-game podcasts
sources.text: At last, Loretta Lynn, Pantera, and Charli XCX are all in the same game With GTA 6 just over a month away from launch, Rockstar has finally started teasing what we can expect from the best part of every Grand Theft Auto game: the radio stations. The studio has revealed a handful of genre-focused stations covering major artists from across the years, and on top of the proper GTA 6 soundtrack , we're also getting a series first in the form of in-game podcasts. You can preview six of the stations in two minute bursts right now, offering a chance to hear a bit of the DJs and brief samplers of the relevant music. There's Cocotea FM, focused on modern Latin music; Back Country Radio, which covers classic outlaw country; Afro Bank FM, offering a wide array of African music; The Chamber 106.6, blasting classic metal; Flash FM, which runs modern pop music; and Dirty South Classics, which will hit your old-school rap and hip-hop needs. These aren't all the stations in the game – the announcement also confirms classic rock and talk radio options – but even this small selection proves that Rockstar is once again going all-out for the soundtrack. Loretta Lynn, Pantera, and Charli XCX all in the same game? That's a premium selection, right there. "Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida's terrestrial radio," Rockstar adds, "with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones." In-game podcasts are hardly a new idea – you can find examples at least as far back as Metal Gear Solid 4 – but it's notable that they're appearing in GTA for the first time here. Admittedly, it's likely not all that different from the talk radio that's been in the series for years, but it is a fun acknowledgement of just how much listening habits have changed since GTA 5 launched back in 2013. I'm not being facetious when I call the radio stations the best part of GTA. I've always loved fake radio banter in games going back to my time playing Streets of SimCity, and Rockstar's talent for music curation has always been impeccable. So many of my memories of playing San Andreas or GTA 4 are tied to specific moments cruising through the world with particular songs blaring over the car radio in the background, and I'm looking forward to making some new ones in GTA 6. Check out our guide to all the GTA 6 cars we know about so far if you want to know what you'll be cruisin' in. sources.text: GTA 6 will let you listen to radio stations while not in a car, by wearing headphones and earbuds connected to smartphones. GTA 6 also introduces on-demand podcasts, so you can binge true crime while also doing true crime - something like that. "For the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto 6 introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida's terrestrial radio," Rockstar wrote on its website , "with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones." Rockstar announced these additions while detailing six of radio stations coming to GTA 6, which appear to be hosted by incredibly famous real-world singers ( according to Rolling Stone ), while offering musical previews of what we'll hear there . It's an incredibly expensive line-up for a game that has been made with no expense spared. As Christian Donlan noted after watching Netflix's extended GTA 6 reveal: this is what a billion dollars gets you . The timing of this GTA 6 announcement coincides with another huge GTA 6 gameplay footage leak by CyberLeek , which shows nudity, dirt-biking and a developer menu. CyberLeek activity had seemed to have stopped following Rockstar parent company Take-Two taking legal action to track them down and find them, but this latest development suggests they're still at large. Meanwhile, GTA 6 edges ever closer to its 19th November release, while Rockstar Games also fights an employment tribunal case in Scotland linked to alleged union busting .

sources.title: DAVE THE DIVER DLC ‘Subnautica 2 Content Pack’ announced
sources.text: MINTROCKET has announced DAVE THE DIVER ‘s final downloadable content pack—a Subnautica 2 -themed expansion in partnership with Unknown Worlds Entertainment . It will launch free of charge in early 2027. “For our final [downloadable content] expansion, we wanted to create something that felt especially meaningful, and a Subnautica collaboration is what players have been asking us about for a long time,” said MINTROCKET studio director Jaeho Hwang in a press release. “Both games are set underwater, but Subnautica has such a distinct approach to underwater exploration, so working with the Subnautica 2 team gave us a chance to bring a new wave to DAVE THE DIVER experience. We’re really excited for players to see what we’ve been working on, and we hope this collaboration gives them one more fresh and surprising adventure with Dave and his friends, old and new.” Subnautica 2 creative director Anthony Gallegos added, “We’re so excited to collaborate with the team at MINTROCKET. It’s clear that we both adore one another’s games a lot, and the expansion is a love letter to both DAVE THE DIVER and the Subnautica universe. People are in for a treat.” The free expansion will see players explore the strange new waters of Proteus, filled with unfamiliar creatures and valuable resources waiting to be discovered. The upcoming Subnautica 2 Content Pack creates a confluence of mysterious waters unlike anything before, with Dave and Bancho traveling interdimensionally to make new discoveries, unlock strange and exotic recipes, and lend a hand to new friends in need—all while facing periodic confrontations with the perilous Leviathan. DAVE THE DIVER is available now for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , Switch 2 , PlayStation 4 , Xbox One , Switch , PC via Steam , Epic Games Store , and Microsoft Store , iOS, and Android.

sources.title: "It's clear that we both adore one another's games a lot" - Dave the Diver and Subnautica 2 team up for a crossover made in heaven
sources.text: At today's Triple-i Showcase , Dave the Diver studio Mintrocket announced a surprisingly obvious, and perfectly fitting, collaboration. The game's final DLC, set for release in early 2027, brings the worlds of Subnautica 2 and Dave the Diver together. Although the two games share deep-sea exploration as a mechanic, they're at opposite ends of the spectrum tonally - though they're still a better fit than many of the other brands Dave the Diver has crossed over with. These have included Balatro, Yakuza, Godzilla, and Guilty Gear to name a few. The upcoming Subnautica 2 DLC is free and was developed in collaboration with Subnautica 2 team Unknown Worlds. It brings Subnautica 2's ocean moon of Proteus to Dave the Diver, and sees Dave and Bancho - having discovered all species of sea creatures and associated sushi recipes in this dimension - travel to a new dimension to uncover more. While there, yes, they're going to run into Subnautica 2's iconic Leviathan, but also make new friends and hopefully return home having made a lot of new discoveries. Jaeho Hwang, Mintrocket studio director said: "Both games are set underwater, but Subnautica has such a distinct approach to underwater exploration, so working with the Subnautica 2 team gave us a chance to bring a new wave to Dave the Diver experience." Subnautica 2 creative director Anthony Gallegos added: "It’s clear that we both adore one another’s games a lot, and the expansion is a love letter to both Dave the Diver and the Subnautica universe. People are in for a treat." The Subnautica 2 x Dave the Diver crossover DLC is available to wishlist on Steam now. Subnautica 2, which launched in early access this year, has been incredibly successful. It sold more than 5 million copies in under a month, convincing publisher Krafton - which was embroiled in a legal battle with studio founders before launch - to turn it into a "franchise IP" .

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Subnautica 2 fans can finally hunt and kill those pesky Nibbler Mangos—in Dave the Diver's crossover DLC
sources.text: I will kill them. I will cook them. I will serve them. Thanks, Dave. It took a while but there's finally an official way to hunt and kill some of Subnautica 2's most annoying sea creatures. The only catch is, you'll have to do it in Dave the Diver DLC—though as catches go, that's a pretty fun one. The crossover was announced today at the Triple-I Initiative showcase. Coming in early 2027, the Dave the Diver X Subnautica 2 content pack will suck Dave into the alien waters of Unknown Worlds' survival game where he can mine resources, hunt fish, and—one would hope—discover some tasty new sushi recipes for Bancho to cook up. Here's the trailer: What caught my eye even more than the glimpse of a massive and intimidating boss at the end of the trailer were those pesky Nibbler Mangos, which start biting you the second you dive into Subnautica 2 and never really stop. Players having no way to kill large enemies in Subnautica 2 has been a bit of a controversy , with some even resorting to mods so they can fight back. It's nice that players can finally get a bit of revenge against those relentless fish, albeit in another game. "We're thrilled to see Subnautica 2's creatures, including the Nibbler Mango, join Dave's world," Mintrocket told PC Gamer via email. "The team had a lot of fun bringing these creatures into our game, and players can expect the DLC to play just like the Dave the Diver they know and love." As for those saddened to hear this is the final DLC for Dave the Diver, that doesn't necessarily mean it's the definitive end of his adventures. "While this will be the final major DLC for Dave the Diver, there may still be smaller content updates or collaborations based on player feedback and our internal plans," Mintrocket told PC Gamer. "Since we're not moving straight into a sequel, we'll keep thinking about ways to make sure players don't forget Dave and his friends." Bancho the Chef, meanwhile, is getting his own game , a prequel, though a release date has yet to be announced. sources.text: New DLC is coming to Dave the Diver and it’s set to be another crossover, with the world of Subnautica 2 set to be woven into the title. Dave the Diver has had a wealth of DLC released since it first came out in 2023, with the MintRocket title collaborating with the likes of the Like a Dragon series, alongside free updates tied to Dredge and Godzilla. Now, Dave is set for another adventure after the announcement of upcoming DLC tied to Subnautica 2, which was announced at the Triple-i Showcase. A key detail revealed is that the upcoming DLC is free and was created in collaboration with Unknown Worlds, the studio behind Subnautica 2, which will see Dave and co. visit a new dimension and travel to Subnautica 2’s ocean moon, Proteus. Speaking about the collaboration, Jaeho Hwang, Mintrocket’s studio director, said: “Both games are set underwater, but Subnautica has such a distinct approach to underwater exploration, so working with the Subnautica 2 team gives us a chance to bring a new wave to the Dave the Diver experience.” Subnautica 2’s creative director Anthony Gallegos added: “It’s clear we both adore one another’s games a lot, and the expansion is a love letter to both Dave the Diver and the Subnautica universe. People are in for a treat.” Launching in early 2027, the Subnautica 2 DLC for Dave the Diver is set to be the game’s final expansion, but it’s unclear whether it will also mark the end of future updates. We do, however, already know it’s not fully the end for the characters introduced in Dave the Diver, as Mintrocket previously announced a separate title for Bancho the Chef, a cooking simulation and adventure game. sources.text: I play so many sweaty action games that pit me against insanely difficult bosses and require the most tight reaction times imaginable that it actually takes quite a lot to get me to pay attention these days. I’ll admit that when I first saw the Phantom Blade Zero gameplay trailers, I didn’t immediately get the hype. After all, this sword-wielding parry-happy action game exists in an era where we get at least a dozen of these a year. It only took about five minutes with developer S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero to see how it sets itself apart, though, with the most smooth and satisfying action since Sekiro, a surprising number of things to do and secrets to find while exploring each level, and a story that seems like it’ll go harder than I expected it to. After over six hours bum-rushing my way through the first leg of the adventure, I left utterly champing at the bit to play more, and have now joined the ranks of those who count this among their most anticipated games of 2026. The thing that immediately jumped out at me about this finely honed action game is just how much it effortlessly oozes style. One cutscene has a character played by Donny Yen balancing a baby on the edge of his blade while he fights off numerous attackers, one boss encounter involved me fighting (and eventually taking on the form of) one of those awesome dancing lions you see in Chinatown on Chinese New Year – even the first few minutes have your character choosing which heart he wants to receive from a creepy ghost monster guy just to make sure you know that the game you’re playing is metal as hell. It’s honestly pretty hard to make your action game with a cool swordmaster protagonist fighting off hordes of monsters stand apart from all the others given how common this trope is at this point, and yet I don’t think there was any point in my time playing where I went more than half an hour without running into something I hadn’t seen before. It’s incredibly impressive stuff! That’s all without getting to the combat itself, which is without question the star of the show here. I don’t think there was even one second of Phantom Blade Zero where I didn’t feel like a complete badass. Some of the many examples I encountered include: riding atop a horse-drawn wagon while fighting off armed pursuers and blocking their gunfire with your sword, killing off enemies with absolutely brutal finishers after you’ve broken their guard meter with repeated parries, and keeping two enemies at bay on either side of you by executing an absurdly cool double kick at the same time. This game has an incredible knack for making you feel like you’re the only person in the world who could have pulled something like that off, and a lot of that is in how smooth the parry mechanics and attack combos are. I surprised myself by how often I was able to do crazy things like parry three thrown daggers in quick succession, then follow it up with a series of attacks that sent me flipping through the air and spinning gracefully as I smacked around enemies like it was nothing, even though most were no slouches themselves. I’m a bit of a snob when it comes to action games, so if the parry windows aren’t just right, or the attacks don’t feel quite satisfying in some imperceptible way, I tend to become disenchanted really quickly. But Phantom Blade Zero gets so many of those tiny details just right, making it incredibly hard to put down. And if the core ways in which the combat feels satisfying are what pulled me in, then the fact that I was able to experience it all over again from a new framing thanks to the bevy of melee weapons was what held my interest. I don’t know how many weapons this thing has or if all of them are as unique as what I got my hands on in this section of the adventure, but just about every weapon of destruction I tried out felt extremely bespoke. I got one massive, two-handed blade by defeating an optional secret boss that carried me to victory through a ton of encounters thanks to its ability to deal an insane amount of damage, while another boss who was a drunken fighting master awarded me with his drunken fighting style after his defeat, which allowed me to bob and weave like a champ, moving unpredictably as I guided my blade telekinetically in front of me, even able to send it flying at the enemy as a ranged weapon. The differences between these kinds of weapons were so stark that it took a ton of time to adjust to each one, learning the combos available to me alongside the pros and cons of using each one as I went, and that went an incredibly long way to help keep my attention as I sliced through the 100th minion enemy in half an hour. There’s also a surprising amount to upgrade as you master your kung fu skills, whether it’s enhancing weapons by investing materials in them to improve their stats and capabilities, or by investing in the various paths of the skill tree, which offer everything from active abilities like one that allows you to interrupt your own attacks to execute a quick dodge out of the way, to passive perks like one that restores your Sha-Chi (used to perform certain special actions) faster than normal. For an action game that’s mostly focused on pulling off sick kills, there’s a surprising amount of RPG that’s snuck its way into the mix here, and I’m all for it. It’s nice to have breaks from combat to do some good old fashioned buildcrafting, even if it didn’t seem to go all that deep from what I saw. Boss fights can make or break a game like Phantom Blade Zero, so it’s a good thing that just about every one I played was an absolute banger. While most of the early fights were pretty bog standard stuff, like a hooded man throwing chained blades at me, or a big burly monstrosity swinging an ax the size of a grown man, it wasn’t long before some more interesting and original ideas took center stage. sources.title: Phantom Blade Zero Preview—This Might Be My Game Of The Year
sources.text: I’ve now had the chance to spend almost 10 hours with Phantom Blade Zero across two back-to-back preview events. The first came at Gamescom this summer, but shortly after that, I was flown out to China to get a closer look behind the scenes and soak up even more hands-on time with S-Game’s breakout title. Ten hours is a long time to spend with a game, and both of my previews essentially gave me free rein to explore. I sat down, hit New Game, and, aside from being whisked away to some late-game bosses towards the end, got to freely experience the opening five hours of Phantom Blade Zero—twice. You’d think that, after replaying the same opening sections almost back-to-back, I’d be dreading playing through them for a third time when the game launches on October 29. The reality, however, couldn’t be further from it. Phantom Blade Zero is simply an insanely good action game, and for reasons I’ll dive into below, I haven’t stopped thinking about it since I got home. There’s an age-old saying that something can have style over substance, quality over quantity, with games often prioritising one over the other. When you play Phantom Blade Zero, however, it’s obvious that S-Game hasn’t held back on either, with its combat oozing just as much flair as it does mechanical depth. That notion becomes immediately apparent in the game’s opening act, and while I can’t reveal what sets the story in motion, it’s clear from the outset that Phantom Blade Zero is prepared to deliver both blockbuster action and jaw-dropping spectacle in equal measure. That philosophy carries throughout the rest of the game, too, and I genuinely can’t stress enough how fluid the action feels. I can attest firsthand to how much effort S-Game has put into its motion capture, with kung-fu legend Donnie Yen serving not only as the Gold Masked One, but also as the head of the game’s mocap team. Every action feels simultaneously believable and supernatural, regardless of which weapon you’re wielding. And there are plenty to choose from, with 30 weapons planned for the game. I got to try around 10 of them during my previews, and each one genuinely altered my playstyle to some degree, with their own unique animations and movesets. It’s an impressive level of variety, especially when those weapons are combined with Phantom Edges, which serve as secondary weapons, and charms. There’s a huge amount of potential for build crafting, and Phantom Blade Zero actively encourages you to experiment. Redirecting your resources into different weapons isn’t difficult, either, meaning you’re never locked into one particular setup. But my favourite part is how you actually obtain some of this new gear: by defeating one of the many bosses. The bosses in Phantom Blade Zero are incredible. In a game so heavily inspired by kung fu, you’d be forgiven for expecting endless fights against samurai and other human warriors. Instead, the variety on display is far more ridiculous—in the best possible way. During my time with the game, I went from fighting Flame, the Lion Dance Grandmaster who spat fireballs at me, to the Lady of the Twin Serpents, a Poison Ivy-esque woman who used towering snakes to zip around the arena and pummel me. And perhaps most excitingly, these encounters are incredibly frequent. The team told me that one of their biggest struggles during development was actually stopping themselves from adding more bosses! The best part is that when you defeat them, you can often acquire the weapons or abilities they were using. Defeat the Lion Dancer, and you’ll get its wearable headpiece, allowing you to shoot fire from its mouth; take down a drunken fighter and you’ll unlock their drunken fighting style, letting protagonist Soul stumble and float through encounters. And that’s without even mentioning the second phases. Every boss has two phases, but don’t worry, this isn’t a soulslike . If you die during the second phase, you’ll skip the first when you return, allowing you to jump straight back into the action in true ARPG fashion. There’s a good chance you will die, because Phantom Blade Zero doesn’t pull its punches. I played on the standard difficulty during my demo, as I didn’t want to lose precious preview time getting stuck on a single encounter. Even then, I was forced to lock in, focus, and give certain fights multiple attempts. When I finally defeated them, it was always super rewarding, though there were occasions when a death didn’t necessarily feel like it was my fault. The build I played suffered from some noticeable stuttering, and in a game this fast-paced, even a momentary hitch could result in a missed parry and a sizeable chunk of my health disappearing. I’m putting some faith in S-Game to have those issues ironed out by launch, though, because when Phantom Blade Zero was running smoothly, which it was the majority of the time, it was a seamless experience. As jaw-dropping as the bosses were, I also really enjoyed exploring Phantom Blade Zero’s vast world. I got to see the first area almost to completion, and the feeling of unlocking new gear that opened previously inaccessible areas, alongside completing side quests for unique rewards, was genuinely satisfying. Partner that with a wuxia-inspired universe and a narrative that doesn’t lean too heavily on Chinese mythological stereotypes, and Phantom Blade Zero is shaping up to be more than just a standard hack-and-slash. The story already seems interesting and approachable, while the world itself feels incredibly rich, with plenty of detail layered into its environments and characters. Although Phantom Blade Zero is technically a semi-open-world game, exploration is also helped by the fact that enemies don’t respawn after you’ve defeated them. It’s a small touch, but it makes clearing out an area feel a little more permanent as you continue your journey. Most people will probably come away from Phantom Blade Zero talking about its spectacular combat and boss fights, and rightfully so.

sources.title: After 4 Hours, Phantom Blade Zero Just Became My Most-Anticipated Action Game
sources.text: From its ‘kungfupunk’ combat to wild boss battles, here’s everything you need to know Action game fans have had no shortage of choice in 2026. Romeo Is a Dead Man spotlights blood-soaked hack-and-slash combat, Beast of Reincarnation offers Souls-adjacent parry-focused fighting, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword takes parrying to the extreme with a plethora of defensive options. Phantom Blade Zero looks to carve out its own space among sword-slashing action games. It blends simple controls and intense parries with stylish wuxia animations to create one of the most anticipated non- GTA 6 games of the fall release calendar. I recently got to play around four hours of Phantom Blade Zero on Windows PC at a preview event hosted by developer S-Game in Beijing, China, and experienced the game’s unique take on melee action. I played from the very beginning of the game until the end of its first chapter. Afterward, I was plopped into two separate boss fights, defeating one and losing against the other. Trading blows with Phantom Blade Zero ’s bosses was certainly the highlight of my time with S-Game’s ambitious martial arts game, though the moment-to-moment action in between those boss fights didn’t reach the same highs. I played as Soul, an assassin being hounded by members of The Order, a shadowy organization he used to work for. Maybe it was the jet lag after a 16.5-hour flight, but I didn’t pick up on that context in the preview; I learned Soul was a John Wick-style assassin on the run when director Soulframe Liang mentioned it during a roundtable interview following the gameplay session. Soul gets mortally wounded fighting his childhood BFF Zuo Shang, and both dudes stab each other through the heart. Don’t worry, Soul doesn't die (yet) — a creepy little guy called the Flesh Sculptor hooks him up with a new heart, but it’ll only last 66 days. Zuo Shang also survives, and now Souls sets off on an action-packed adventure to presumably find and battle his old friend once and for all. Nothing about the story really grabbed me in these opening hours, but, to be frank, the stories of action games like Black Myth: Wukong , Stellar Blade , and Beast of Reincarnation didn’t grab me much either, and I still put dozens of hours into those games. The real crux of Phantom Blade Zero ’s appeal is its combat, which, after the preview session, I look forward to experiencing in full. S-Game’s stated goal is to bring Chinese martial arts to life through Phantom Blade Zero ’s combat. Soulframe wanted to translate the cinema of wuxia films to action-packed gameplay and to “create a playable kung fu movie.” S-Game has recruited movie star and martial artist Donnie Yen to help bring its vision to life as a creative consultant, and he’s even playing and mo-caping a character in the game. Yen leads a team of about 15-20 stunt performers and helps choreograph the action, which is full of the stuntmen performing lightning-fast choreography that sometimes involves wirework stunts, like in wuxia movies. Kenji Tanigaki — best known for directing The Furious , widely considered the best action movie of the year — is a part of Yen’s team as an action director. With Yen, Tanigaki, and more martial arts masters on board, S-Game succeeds in its goal, as every animation has an over-the-top flourish. Soul won’t just advance on an enemy and strike, but whirl his sword around, air trials following it, with a certain panache as he attacks. He won’t just climb up a ledge, but dramatically leap upward and do a little spinny spin to land. Everything about Phantom Blade Zero ’s style is so extra , which lends the game a certain charm, even when frightening monster enemies are barreling down upon you. While Phantom Blade Zero nails the look of kung fu, at the end of the day I’m still just mashing Square and Triangle, cool animation or not. The more I play, the more I discover the combat’s depth, however. Key to that depth is Soul’s Sha-chi meter, which is like a stamina meter for his most powerful combos. In an early boss fight, I learn just how crucial Sha-chi is to the combat. Switching weapons refills the meter, meaning I can exhaust Soul’s Sha-chi with devastating attacks, switch to my other equipped weapon, and keep the party going with a refilled Sha-chi meter. It’s a lot like discovering how transforming your trick weapon mid-combo in Bloodborne can unleash a heavy blow. Boss battles are certainly the highlight of Phantom Blade Zero . Though the cadence of them isn’t as quick as in a game like Black Myth Wukong (which feels more like a boss rush game at times), they still come fast and furious. The combat really shines in tough boss battles, whereas encounters with regular enemies can feel too paint-by-numbers and end too quickly. I lost count of just how many bosses I tackled in the preview, from an enemy on a horse-drawn carriage to a foe who conjures additional arms mid-battle, essentially becoming a sickle-wielding General Grievous. The session concluded with two later-game boss battles, both of which were quite tough. The first was against a woman who flitted on the air and summoned what looked like paper mache dragons from the ground. (I was too busy trying not to die to admire their design.) She was a challenge, and had two phases. Thankfully, an ally joined in for the second phase, and I’m hopeful more boss fights in Phantom Blade Zero will have NPCs fighting alongside Soul. I always enjoy having a partner along for the ride. I only got one attempt at the second boss fight due to time constraints on my play session, but it had some of the most notable sequences in Phantom Blade Zero I saw. I fought against two dancers controlling a lion head puppet; after the first was defeated, the second summoned little enemies, each with their own lion heads. sources.title: New Leadership Appointments and XBOX Division
sources.text: This message was just sent to Team XBOX employees globally. At Town Hall on Tuesday, I talked about the four Cs and the choices we are making to put them into practice. You’ve seen a lot of our work on Core and Content. Today I want to share two leadership appointments supporting Creator and Connection. Kayleen Walters will transition from her role at Mojang to President of XP, a new XBOX division focused on how people experience our franchises beyond the games themselves, and Maria Angelidou-Smith will join XBOX as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft. Both will report to me. Kayleen has spent her career building entertainment franchises. Before XBOX, she spent 13 years at Lucasfilm helping guide Star Wars across films, products, and partnerships. At Minecraft, she helped grow consumer products into a multibillion-dollar business with more than 250 licensees and was Executive Producer of A Minecraft Movie , the biggest film in the U.S. last year and a top-five release worldwide. She is also a producer of the sequel. XP is a play on “Experience Points” and formalizes four investment areas for us: XBOX PICTURES for film and television adaptations; XBOX PRODUCTS for licensing and merchandise; XBOX PARTNERSHIPS for sponsors and brand partners; and XBOX PLACES for our marquee broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences. Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place. Kayleen’s move also gave us time to think carefully about what Mojang needs in its next leader. Minecraft is one of the largest communities in entertainment. Hundreds of millions of people play, build, create, teach, watch, mod, run servers, and build businesses around Minecraft. The community doesn’t just consume the product. It helps shape what the product becomes. That was central to our search. Mojang already has an exceptional game development team that knows Minecraft and its players deeply. We wanted someone who has built products for communities at enormous scale, who is deeply technical, and who understands how creators, product, technology, and monetization come together. Maria brings a rare combination of those experiences. She spent nearly a decade at Meta, where she led Facebook Groups used by more than 1.8 billion people each month, as well as Events, Creators, Search, Profile, and Monetization. She later led product and technology at Personio and served as Chief Product Officer at Reddit, another of the world’s largest community platforms. She has built products used by billions of people and led product and engineering organizations through significant growth and change. Maria brings deep experience to Mojang, along with a respect for what makes Minecraft special. Her first priority will be learning from the teams and communities who know Minecraft best. She starts Monday, October 19. Please join me in congratulating Kayleen and welcoming Maria to XBOX!

sources.title: Xbox announces new XP division to deliver transmedia spinoffs including film, TV, and theme parks
sources.text: The division will be led by former Mojang president Kayleen Walters, who will be replaced by Reddit's Maria Angelidou-Smith Xbox has announced a new XP business unit, dedicated to transmedia brand extensions, including the Fallout TV series and the Minecraft World theme park. The new enterprise will be led by Kayleen Walters, the current president of Minecraft developer Mojang Studios, who previously spent eight years overseeing franchise development at Microsoft. Before joining Microsoft, she spent 13 years at Lucasfilm, rising to become vice president of franchise marketing and integrated planning. Walters was appointed as head of Mojang Studios in February , replacing outgoing head Åsa Bredin, who stepped down to "focus on personal goals outside of work." Walters will be replaced as president of Mojang by Maria Angelidou-Smith, who joins the Xbox division from Reddit, where she was chief product officer. Previously, she spent nearly a decade at Facebook. The XP division will focus on four areas: Xbox Pictures for film and television adaptations, Xbox Products for licensing and merchandise, Xbox Partnerships for sponsors and brand partners, and Xbox Places for broadcast and in-person events, theme parks, and other location-based experiences. In an email sent to Xbox employees this morning, Xbox head Asha Sharma said that the firm's franchises "mean more to people than the time they spend playing them, and Kayleen knows how to build those experiences with the industry without losing what made people care about the franchise in the first place." On Angelidou-Smith's appointment, Sharma said: "We wanted someone who has built products for communities at enormous scale, who is deeply technical, and who understands how creators, product, technology, and monetization come together. Maria brings a rare combination of those experiences." At the recent Minecraft Live event in September, it was announced that the Minecraft World destination will open at UK theme park Chessington World of Adventures in 2027. Microsoft entered a deal with Chessington owner Merlin Entertainments in 2024 , with Merlin investing more than $110 million in two Minecraft-themed attractions. "We are everywhere digitally, Merlin is everywhere physically," said Walters at the time of the deal. "It's about how do we expand Minecraft beyond the game. Mojang and Microsoft are experts on Minecraft and the brand, Merlin are the experts on location-based experiences; it's a shared vision." Walters was executive producer of A Minecraft Movie in 2025, which generated $550 million after ten days in theatres. A sequel has been greenlit for July 23, 2027 . Microsoft's new XP business unit will also oversee the Fallout TV series, which has been a hit for Amazon Prime Video, and has driven increased sales of the franchise's back catalogue , along with a player uptick in mobile title Fallout Shelter. The Halo TV series was less successful, lasting only two seasons on Paramount+ before being cancelled in 2024. A Gears of War movie that will " tell the origin story of Delta Squad " is currently in development at Netflix. The announcement of the new XP division is the latest in a long list of changes in Microsoft's gaming portfolio. Sharma announced a "reset" earlier this year , which has led to the loss of around 3,200 jobs and the divestment of five studios . But GamesIndustry.biz contributing editor Rob Fahey has questioned where the reset is going : "Nobody has yet deigned to outline a clear vision for what Xbox will actually look like after this reset," he said.

XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love. XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations. XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships. XP will be led by Kayleen Walters, who is moving from her role heading up Minecraft -maker Mojang to be president of the new division. Mojang will next be led by Maria Angelidou-Smith, who is leaving her job as Reddit’s chief product officer to become CEO of Mojang and Minecraft , and she starts on October 19th. Xbox is already developing several film and TV adaptations, including a sequel to the successful A Minecraft Movie , a third season of Prime Video’s Fallout live-action series , a Call of Duty film , and a Diablo animated series for Netflix . “Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of XBOX,” Ball says. “XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love.” Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also sent an email about the changes to employees. She had previously told staff that the company would build “long-term plans” for Xbox’s franchises “across film, television, consumer products, sponsorship, live experiences” as part of her broader “reset” of the Xbox business. Since taking over in February, Sharma has enacted sweeping layoffs , sold off studios, and made big changes to Xbox’s studio structure, including putting Activision in charge of Halo . sources.text: Best Buy has announced it will be opening select stores at midnight for the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The major US retailer is gearing up for the highly anticipated release, with its website also now featuring a countdown to November 5. The midnight launch will also include a fresh batch of stock for the limited-edition Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Switch 2 consoles and matching Switch 2 Pro controllers. That's potentially good news for anyone who missed out on the special-edition console during the preorder excitement in September . For now, Best Buy hasn't specified how many systems will be available or which stores will receive stock, but it has warned that quantities are limited. Best Buy has also said that store hours will vary depending on region, so you'll want to check with your local store before heading out. If you already have an Ocarina of Time preorder set for shipping and would prefer to collect it during the midnight opening, Best Buy has said you can also do this by modifying your order through your "Best Buy purchase history". There is a good reason for fans to preorder elsewhere, however, as both Amazon and Walmart have Ocarina of Time listed for $59.88 instead of $69.99 . The special edition Switch 2 console and accessories was shown off during the dedicated Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Direct last month. They will be available from October 29, but are currently sold out at every major retailer in the U.S . Other highlights in the Nintendo Direct included the first gameplay reveal for Ocarina of Time , as well as a release date. This is a full remake of the 1998 Nintendo 64 original game, with overhauled graphics that bring it up to modern standards. According to Nintendo, this is a "faithful interpretation" for new hardware, but it does have a few more lines of dialogue for the characters you meet along the way, to give them more personality. sources.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen review: um RPG completo e com muitos detalhes na jogabilidade
sources.text: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen vale a pena para quem gosta de RPG de mundo aberto com sistemas profundos, peões com personalidade própria e horas e mais horas de exploração, e o preço compensa pela quantidade de conteúdo. Mas se você espera gráficos ultrarrealistas, uma história cheia de reviravoltas ou um jogo que explica tudo de mão beijada, prepare-se: aqui o tempo (o seu e o do jogo) é parte da experiência. Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen é a versão completa do RPG de ação da Capcom lançado em 2024, agora acompanhado de uma expansão inédita ambientada na região de Norgan. O pacote chega em 9 de outubro de 2026 para PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC (Steam) e, pela primeira vez, Nintendo Switch 2, plataforma em que testei o jogo. O primeiro Dragon’s Dogma, de 20212, chegou ao PlayStation 3 e ao Xbox 360 em maio daquele ano, dirigido por Hideaki Itsuno, nome que os fãs de ação conhecem de Devil May Cry . A história começa em Cassardis, uma vila de pescadores no ducado de Gransys, quando um dragão ataca, arranca o coração do protagonista e o deixa vivo. A partir dali, você se torna o Arisen, o escolhido destinado a enfrentar a criatura. A grande sacada do jogo, já naquela época, eram os peões: companheiros controlados pela inteligência artificial que você cria, treina e compartilha com outros jogadores. Um peão seu podia acompanhar a aventura de outra pessoa e voltar com conhecimento novo sobre missões e inimigos. Em abril de 2013, a Capcom lançou Dragon’s Dogma: Dark Arisen , uma versão expandida que juntava o jogo original a um conteúdo novo e bem mais difícil: a Bitterblack Isle, uma ilha-masmorra pensada para o pós-jogo. Foi essa edição que manteve a franquia viva por anos, ganhando versões para PC em 2016, PS4 e Xbox One em 2017 e Nintendo Switch em 2019. No meio do caminho, o Japão recebeu ainda o Dragon’s Dogma Online (2015), um spin-off online que nunca saiu de lá e foi encerrado em 2019, e a Netflix lançou uma adaptação em anime em 2020. A sequência demorou mais de uma década para chegar. Dragon’s Dogma 2 foi lançado em 22 de março de 2024 para PS5, Xbox Series X|S e PC. Nele, você volta a ser o Arisen, mas desperta sem memória, enquanto um impostor ocupa o trono do reino de Vermund. O mapa se divide entre Vermund, terra dos humanos, e Battahl, lar dos beastren. O jogo passou de 4 milhões de cópias vendidas até o fim de 2025 sem receber nenhuma expansão, uma lacuna que finalmente foi preenchida agora. Assim como em 2013, o novo Dark Arisen junta o jogo-base a um conteúdo inédito, e não por acaso: a expansão é dirigida por Kento Kinoshita, o mesmo diretor do Dark Arisen original. Segundo a Capcom , a nova campanha leva o Arisen ao norte, para Norgan, uma região gelada abandonada há muito tempo. Lá, ele encontra o Dragão Caído (Fallen Dragon), uma criatura imortal que está sem o próprio coração, e se une a uma personagem misteriosa chamada Eir para investigar os segredos dela. O espelho com o primeiro jogo é claro: se antes era o Arisen quem perdia o coração para um dragão, agora é o dragão quem vaga sem ele. Além da campanha, a expansão traz 12 masmorras de desafio, chamadas Lost Rites, que recompensam com equipamentos raros, e relíquias encontradas na exploração de Norgan, que podem ser avaliadas por NPCs específicos para forjar armas e armaduras mais fortes, algumas com efeitos e habilidades únicas. O editor de personagens também ganhou novos penteados e tatuagens. O visual de Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen não é nada impressionante no Nintendo Switch 2. É o padrão de um RPG desse porte, em que o que importa mais é a mecânica e a história do que gráficos extremamente avançados. Quem chega esperando um espetáculo visual de nova geração vai se decepcionar, mas quem conhece a proposta da série sabe que o foco nunca esteve aí. As cutscenes, por outro lado, são bem feitas e cumprem bem o papel de dar peso aos momentos da história. Joguei no Nintendo Switch 2, no modo portátil, com todas as configurações no máximo. O jogo roda a no máximo 30 FPS, com o FSR 3 Frame Generation ligado. A Capcom confirmou que essa é a primeira vez que usa geração de quadros num jogo de Switch 2: o recurso interpola imagens para chegar a algo equivalente a 60 FPS, e pode ser ligado ou desligado a qualquer momento. Durante a jogatina em si, não percebi travamentos ou dificuldades. O único ponto que me incomodou foram algumas cutscenes que demoraram a entrar, dando a impressão de que o console precisava de mais tempo para carregá-las. O mundo de Dragon’s Dogma 2 é aberto, e você vai aceitando diversas missões ao longo da jornada. E aqui vai o primeiro conselho: cuidado para não acumular missões demais e esquecer as que dependem do tempo. Um exemplo: ao chegar a Vernworth, a capital de Vermund, recebi uma missão para entrar no castelo e encontrar uma pessoa. Só que isso só era para ser feito à meia-noite. Não existe um relógio na tela marcando o prazo, mas também não dá para enrolar e esperar o dia raiar. Essa passagem de tempo influencia diversas situações. Pessoas que ficam num lugar durante o dia podem estar em outro à noite. Para avançar as horas, você pode se hospedar numa pousada ou usar bancos especiais espalhados por alguns locais. A noite tem regras próprias. Você precisa de uma lamparina para enxergar no escuro, o que também ajuda a localizar – e ser localizado pelo – os monstros, e, nas áreas selvagens, encontra criaturas diferentes das que aparecem durante o dia. Até os itens sentem o tempo passar. Uma maçã, por exemplo, pode amadurecer, envelhecer e virar itens diferentes para a combinação de materiais. Os alimentos crus pedem atenção redobrada, para que você não acabe consumindo algo velho ou podre que traga efeitos colaterais. Essa foi a parte em que achei a explicação do jogo mais fraca. Há uma variedade enorme de itens, e você acaba tendo que fazer combinações na sorte para descobrir novos objetos. sources.title: Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen impresses more than the original RPG's DLC as per Metacritic score
sources.text: Dragon's Dogma 2 is back in the limelight now after its 2024 launch thanks to its Dark Arisen DLC, which lands tomorrow – and is apparently superior to its 2013 predecessor. A whopping 13 years ago now, the original Dragon's Dogma RPG from Capcom got its own Dark Arisen expansion, and admittedly, I loved it. Everything from the Bitterblack Isle to the formidable foes the DLC boasted had me in a chokehold – and this week, the new Dragon's Dogma 2 Dark Arisen content threatens to do the same. And, what's more, it appears to be impressing critics more than its decade-old predecessor did. Over on Metacritic , the Dragon's Dogma 2 Dark Arisen expansion boasts a solid score of 84. That's pretty dang good, and the small snippets provided from reviews solidify as much. One outlines how the DLC has "made Dragon's Dogma 2 a must-play RPG," for example, while others say it accomplishes what the original game's own follow-up content did and then some – so, yeah. It seems as though it's shaping up to be quite a time. As for the original Dragon's Dogma and its own Dark Arisen DLC… well, it's got a score of 81 on the platform. That's not bad at all, but it's notably a few points under its successor, which is exciting. The new take on Dark Arisen's chaos is mere hours away at this point, so I do also wonder what fans will think of it. For reference, the OG expansion's got a "user score" of 7.9 – will tomorrow's prove even higher? I certainly hope so. We're talking everything from enhanced gameplay to new adventures in snowy, unforgiving Norgan and even an improved character creator, as though I didn't spend enough time in it a couple years back. All that's left to do now is wait, I suppose. If you've not preordered it yet yourself, Dark Arisen is live on Steam and other platforms for $30 – a small price to pay, should critics' thoughts on the DLC so far ring true. sources.text: Time management mystery adventure game Trainwatch will launch for PC via Steam on March 10, 2027, publisher 11 bit studios and developer Harvester Games announced. “ Trainwatch might be the most mechanics-heavy of my games, but the gist of psychological horror is still very much there, and underlies everything,” said solo developer Rem Michalski in a press release. “It’s a more nuanced kind of horror than explicit violence and jump scares. It’s about an unsettling experience, a claustrophobic setting, and internal, human traumas.” Here is an overview of the game, via 11 bit studios: In Trainwatch , you’ll experience the rush of memorizing the train timetable and closing and raising the gate. You’ll also have to keep an eye on your hunger meter, get a good amount of sleep, and make sure to keep your hands washed after any bathroom breaks so you don’t get sick. As you progress, you’ll unlock new skills and abilities, all the while being drawn further and further into the fog surrounding the Tower. Strangers ask for help or a conversation, incoming trains carry messages, and the weirdness spins faster and faster. But be warned, the clock keeps ticking: a day can’t be stretched, and not every lead can be chased, or every promise kept. If you want to fix your life in a month, you’ll need to decide what matters most and learn to let go.
